recipes.name: Apricot Almond Galette
ingredients_raw: 1 (9 inch) refrigerated pie crust (such as Pillsbury®)
10 small fresh apricots, pitted and quartered

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Roll out pie crust onto a baking sheet.
Toss apricots with white sugar in a bowl until evenly coated; set aside.

Combine almond meal, confectioners' sugar, and egg in a separate bowl until paste-like; spread onto center of pie crust, leaving ½ inch bare crust around edges. Arrange sugared apricots on top almond paste.
Fold ½-inch bare crust edge inward over almond paste and apricots, leaving center of galette uncovered. Crimp crust edges with a fork.
Bake in the preheated oven until crust is golden brown, about 40 minutes. Brush melted apricot jam over galette. Slice; serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Apricot Almond Galette
raw_recipe.description: Fresh, sweet apricots are baked with a delicious almond paste in this apricot almond galette recipe. Use homemade pastry or a store-bought pie crust.

review.reviewBody: This was a very nice, not too sweet dessert, that went together quickly. The only changes to be made in the future are: 1. More apricots 2. Baked in a tart pan, with removable bottom 3. Oven temp. 375 and check the pie every 7 min. after 1/2 hour. I used a small knife to test if the apricots were softened. 4. Did not need to glaze afterward. This was truly a delicious dessert and, perfect if you wish something sweet after a meal, without a lot of heaviness

I’m happy I found this recipe. I was gifted some home grown apricots & didn’t know what to do with them. I made this with a couple tweaks. For the sugar in the apricots I used 1/2 Splenda & 1/2 granulated sugar just to cut back on the sugar. I also used an Apricot Pineapple jam & almond flour as that’s what I had on hand. I felt the jam really added allot. The recipe was very easy to follow and came out very good. I didn’t snap a pic but it came out almost as pretty as pictured. I plan to make it again.

My only change is I made my pie crust. Can't use store- bought, most have soy!Love it and now sad cause apricots are gone until next year in NJ. Well hubby and I needed another. I just made a second because apricots are gone I just used canned apricot halves. WOW real good . Fruit backed in juice. Drained well & tried to dry them on a tea towel. Tossed with 1 tablespoons of cornstarch mixed with the sugar. When you gotta gave it you'll try anything.

I made a tart. My neighbor gave me some apricots from her tree. At first, I tried peeling the apricots using the hot water method, but they were hard anyway, so since I was just making this for myself, I made it with some peeled and some unpeeled. The tart was ok without peeling the apricots Yum! The apricots were great! I used the apricot jam glaze. I ate the first slice without the glaze, then glazed it. The apricots in the jam filled the gaps where there were some, and was not too sweet. So you can leave the glaze off if you want, but I liked the glaze, and it gave the tart a nice finish.
Loved the recipe. I use medium apricots and sliced thinner. The use of a premature crust speeded up the process.

I made this exactly as written but didn't like the texture of the almond paste using the almond meal it tasted gritty I think I would make my own with ground almonds also I like my desserts sweeter adding the jam does help with that a little bit..
good, but my apricots were too juicy and I had to remove some liquid near the end. (maybe I will add a little cornstarch to the sugar apricot mixture next time to firm it up.

Easy, especially if you made it more than once.
I made my own almond paste just grounding up almonds in the food processor.
Easy and delicious. I made this without the jam.
I did not use the jam. It was very good. Not much trouble and pretty!
